notes.title: Who Wants To Play? - 1st Playtest Session is now live!
notes.content:
Hey Ritualists!

We're officially opening a public playtest for all of you gamers! We're really excited to show you what we've been working on so far :)

Here's what you can look forward to!
- 4 Unique Playable Guns
- 20+ Unlockable Spells
- Fully Playable Level 1 (Still prone to changes)
- Boss Fight Unlocked
- Out-of-run progression systems in unlocking and upgrading Spells

Just so you know, the game's current state is still very early and in the process of being further optimised. We have a ton of improvements planned, but for now, we would love to hear your feedback! 
There is a survey button found in our game's pause menu and death screen to share your thoughts on how else the experience can be improved. Your feedback is very important to us, so please we're all ears!

If you love our game and want to be part of the community, then also consider joining our Discord!


Cheers!
The Ritual Chamber Team

notes.title: Devlog #3 - New Foes & Features
notes.content:
Hey Ritualists!
We’re back with another exciting update on Ritual Chambers! There’s a lot brewing behind the scenes, and today, we’re diving into even more features in development. Let’s get into it.

More Deadly Foes Await
The world of Ritual Chambers is getting more dangerous with new adversaries:

 Attestants (Marble Hand) – A mysterious entity with imposing presence and eerie movements.
 Flametender (Candle Monster) – A spectral enemy wielding the power of fire, lighting up the battlefield in sinister ways.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183707/908a77e4071d57c646bcc19a26b1103d4815eaa5.jpg

Enemies are also being fine-tuned for better encounters:

 Smoother animations & attack exaggeration – Enemies will have more defined movements, making dodging and countering feel even more rewarding.
 Warding VFX – More visual feedback for enemy abilities to make battles visually distinct. 

Level Design Evolution
We’re making the world of Ritual Chambers even more immersive with:
 A new aesthetic overhaul for environments, enhancing the game’s dark fantasy atmosphere.
 Level Mechanics to encourage strategic play and add smooth game flow, like doors unlocking upon clearing a room.
 Loot randomization – Smash breakables, open chests, and uncover hidden resources.
 Rune Pedestal mechanic – A minor level mechanic that can trigger an explosion using mana.
 Crystals Improvements – Crystal orbs now home in on you instead of requiring manual pickup.
 Ammo Boxes – Tweaked visuals so they fit naturally into the environment without being overly bright. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183707/a071816edf51f65930df91b72571412320f31099.gif

The Divine Organon - Unlocking Your Potential
Progression is expanding with a powerful new system: the Divine Organon.
 This system rewards investment, allowing players to upgrade spells by gaining Aspect Levels.
 The more you invest, the greater your mastery over magic, unlocking new ways to customize and optimize your builds.
 Experience is gained naturally by using spells and dealing damage, making progression feel fluid and rewarding.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183707/c31384600ac53aa8951d0b02dee071715770a3da.gif

Expanding Spell & Build Customization
We’re bringing even more depth to build crafting through the Sigil system: 
 Each spell now has two Sigil slots, granting passive effects.
 Example: Kicking could summon a rock projectile, adding a unique twist to movement.
 Sigils can be earned by fighting enemies, breaking crystals, or found in chests.
 Higher Aspect Rank unlocks more Sigils, rewarding progression with greater build variety. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183707/db5c3ee98aac81be48a937cc30412d28588f7e7f.gif

Karmic Conduit - Persistent Progression
Outside of individual runs, the Karmic Conduit system is shaping up to enhance long-term growth:
 Earn Karma by slaying specific enemies or completing unique actions.
 Spend Karma on blessings that provide lasting benefits, such as:

 Boosting health and mana.
 Reducing the cost of high-tier spells.
 Starting with multiple spells instead of just one. 
The system ensures each run builds toward greater power, giving more incentives to experiment with different playstyles.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183707/4c7a92a2830bb361ee863675d97bde87d99e1bf2.gif

UI & UX Overhaul
The UI has been upgraded once again! More intuitive navigation, improved notifications, and a fresh design overhaul (upcoming) bring a cleaner and more immersive experience. Spell icons have been updated too, now featuring simpler, more recognizable silhouettes to help you at a glance.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183707/d195cc02b3713ffe2831c3fee84182eafd274e48.gif

That’s all for this update, but there’s still plenty more in development! We’re excited to keep refining Ritual Chambers and bringing even more depth to the game.
As always, thank you for your support and enthusiasm. Stay tuned for more!

All the best,
B, Main Dev
Ritual Chambers

notes.title: Devlog #2 - Major changes
notes.content:
Hi everyone!
Back with another devlog, and there's plenty to be excited about! Since our last update, we’ve been hard at work refining Ritual Chamber, adding new mechanics, expanding the spell roster, and enhancing the game’s overall feel. Let’s dive right in!

New Spells & Expanded Magic
The spell arsenal has grown significantly, with a mix of buffs and spells that use new mechanics. Here’s a glimpse of some of the latest additions:

 Oversurge (Sorcery) – Release a shockwave that explodes spell constructs and projectiles, inflicting the Feedback debuff on entities.
 Soul Predator (Sorcery) – Fire a volley of homing projectiles that reward Mana with each that lands.
 Fulminate (Sorcery) – Bullets struck create nodes of lightning that strike each other and nearby entities.
 Bonebreaker (Fleshmithing) –.Struck entities have their bones pulled out of them. Breaking those bones leaves them bleeding.
 Succor of the Departed (Fleshmithing) – A Ritual Spell. Bleeding entities and corpses within periodically release a homing heal bolt.
 Catapult (Druidy) – Kick a boulder that erupts into an earthy impact or launch yourself, leaving behind a shockwave.

This is just a portion of what’s being worked on—expect even more variety in future updates!

Worldbuilding & Level Design Enhancements
Ritual Chambers is becoming even more immersive, with environmental lore being fleshed out to give deeper meaning to locations and adversaries. While not yet fully integrated, expect worldbuilding elements to shape the atmosphere and narrative.
Aesthetic Overhaul – Levels are being redesigned for better visual cohesion.
New mechanics:

 Kill-to-open doors – Clear all enemies to unlock paths.
 Randomized loot – More destructible objects and hidden caches.
 Rune Pedestal mechanic – Stand on a pedestal to charge an explosive effect.
 Crystal orb system – Crystals now home in on you automatically.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183707/a4b8be19ca2ef39e2cc4082b1a01cb6e15a5ee7d.png

Progression Systems: Divine Organon & Karmic Conduit
Two major systems are being developed to add long-term progression:

 Divine Organon – A progression tree where Aspect Levels allow for spell upgrades, earned through combat and spell usage.
 Karmic Conduit – A new out-of-run system where accumulating Karma (through kills, actions, and quests) lets you unlock blessings that enhance your base attributes, improve spell efficiency, and expand your starting spell choices.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183707/b81751eea79e6121abf8844e619d64626e1132a5.gif

Movement Tweaks
Dashing has been improved to feel faster and sharper—perfect for those who love quick, sudden escapes or aggressive repositioning.

New Enemies & Boss Encounters
The horrors within Ritual Chambers continue to evolve. We’ve added brand-new enemies, a mini-boss, and a main boss—each bringing unique challenges. Combat pacing has been tuned to feel more intense, with enemies dealing greater damage but having lower health to keep fights deadly and engaging.
Knock-back system – A new mechanic where dealing enough damage can stagger enemies, inspired by Soulslike poise mechanics.
New enemy movements – More exaggerated attack animations, better telegraphs, and refined behavior.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183707/b9c52f942ead1cbd28bad0bdf80a05af700122a1.gif

Expanded Arsenal: More Guns & Variants
Guns are getting a much-needed boost (and more upcoming)! We’ve updated four new firearms: 

 Inquisitor (Assault Rifle)  
 Homage (Pistol)  
 First Promise (Revolver) 
 Fervor (Shotgun) 

Each firearm will also have stat variations, encouraging different playstyles and loadout experimentation.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183707/7d38d1667c33e116516b10f517f02e03f3541e73.jpg

Where the game’s at?
We’ve made big strides since the last Dev log, which was…already a few months back. Wow. Anyways, I’m a little stressed but hopeful about he current state of the game! Namely, optimisation and creating background systems have been unexpectedly challenging. 

As it is, though, the first level of the game and a good amount of the main progression systems have been settled! The core game loop is implemented, we have a good amount of starting spells, and the environment and VFX are looking good! I’m especially happy about having the Boss fight and spell levelling system in place.

Next up is completing planned level mechanics, sprinkling the nuggets of the background lore we’ve been cooking, and, of course, introducing new firearms and spells! 

These are just some of the highlights! More features are in development, and there’s plenty more to come as Ritual Chamber continues to evolve. Let us know what excites you the most, and stay tuned for future devlogs!


See you in the depths, 
B 
Ritual Chambers Main Dev

notes.title: Devlog #1 - The First of Many
notes.content:
Hi everyone! 

I figured it's time I got around to introducing myself, and to provide some updates on the game. Starting this week, I'm going to begin posting devlogs on Ritual Chambers, so all of you get an idea on what's being produced, and how much you can expect when the game demo is finally released! 

So hi, I'm the main dev of Ritual Chambers, and here's a rundown on the game's progress.

Recent Changes

UI Overhaul

Firstly, the earliest amongst you guys would notice the UI looked much more "old school" and boxy before. After some internal feedback, I've decided it could use a makeover. To give it a more on-theme and clean layout, I've changed it to a more "ritualistic" and dark fantasy aesthetic. 

I also finally got rid of the old placeholder spell icons I got from some asset, and updated it with cleaner and "grungier" icons. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183707/69d63f3554f5612e8a5b6b39257d3025723959ab.png

I'm also a big fan of diegetic menus and thematic aesthetics, so the Binding Altar's UI gets a huge upgrade as well! I've also made the UX more intuitive. In the old UI, my playtesters kept having issues getting to the fun part of the game, where they gain new spells and started casting. The new UI should be a lot easier to navigate now. Also, it looks cooler. (imo)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183707/4f0ae59a6db4742ab9b4cf732875a698e126fa9a.png

Ammo System

You may have noticed it in the earlier image, but yes, we have an ammo system now!

As a developer, I want my players to have fun and have to freedom to be as wizardy as they want, with a higher focus on mana management rather than the usual FPS aspects. I realized I wanted wrong.

A few playtesters brought up the issue that the gunplay may be too monotonous and the game lacked dynamism. Before, you essentially had infinite ammo with any gun, though you need to reload. Since you could essentially empty your magazine and kill stuff with no repercussions, this made spells less useful, which is basically blasphemy.

In the end, I caved in and implemented an ammo system. Now, firearms will require ammo, with ammo being separated into three types:

 Light Bits: High fire-rate firearms, like assault Rifles and submachine guns. etc.
 Heavy Leads: Low fire-rate but high damage firearms, like pistols, revolvers, shotguns, etc.
 Esoteric Scuds: Firearms with variable damage and add-on effects. Rarest ammo type.


Additionally, I can place ammo as a form of loot around the map, incentivising a need to explore, and adding some dynamic flow to combat. 

I hadn't implemented guns with Esoteric Scuds yet, but I have plans to include more than the usual guns you see in FPS. I'd love to really get creative with some fantasy gun designs. Maybe a firearm made of floating bones, or a squirt gun with a jar of detached alien eyes, or some other cool thing like that. Honestly, the specific designs are still confined to the drawing board!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183707/cabfe40285c048af24282b51f5070660b25f0421.gif

New Spells

My personal favourite part of the game, both as a game dev and fantasy enjoyer. If you're like me, and like variety and creating builds, you'll be happy to hear that I'm designing the spells with that intent in mind. I want to give you guys the whole palette, not just 66 differently coloured fireballs and encourage mixing spells and firearms, so you guys have all the ammo to optimise your builds with.

A quick rundown on some of the spells in Ritual Chambers, including ones already implemented.


 Wisps: Shots are turned into lightning wisps that float in the air based on how its fired, firing lightning at nearby enemies.
 Gust Bubble: Your next shot release a windy shockwave, knocking back all nearby enemies and creating a temporary wind dome barrier in the area.
 Desecrate: Shots fired at a corpse consumes the corpse, and results in a large explosion.
 Napalm: Fireball.
 Soul Metabolism: While the spell is active, Rune Counter (a combo mechanic) regenerates your health instead of mana.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183707/c586f582e9b453b21e99734983e00842312377e9.gif

Where's the game at?

Currently, I feel the game is still quite early. While I'm very happy with game's current look and base systems, there is much more content to be implemented before it's ready to be played. I want the game to be a truly satisfying experience for you guys, and that means replayability, catering to different playstyles, intuitive UI, fun-to-explore rooms, and so on. 

The game has most of the base systems established:

 Gun-casting System: Equipping guns or spells, enchanting spells unto guns, and various other spell types and bullet-hit interactions
 Level Generation: Room pooling system, where each run involves going through a randomised set of environments.
 Resource Management: Rune Counters and Ammo, the main systems that generates the resources the Player needs to fight.
 Spellbinding: Finding and interacting with a Binding Altar lets the Player spend affinity (gained throughout the level) to gain Spells for that run.
 Sigils: In-run passive abilities that further adds to build variation.
 Blessings: Out-of-run progression system. Gain passive abilities and stat increases that remains throughout the game.


I'm a big fan of making builds in RPGs, large variety in abilities, open exploration and dark fantasy, which might be apparent in the game's design. It's kind of a passion of mine to truly explore what I create with a magic system, and Ritual Chamber is my first big step in doing that, so I hope you all like what you see!

Future plans

This include the main things Ritual Chambers need to be a proper viable game. Well, this is half things the game needs, and half things I want to put in the game. Here's a list of things I plan to implement by the time the early access is out.


 More guns: The current roster of 3 guns is pathetic. At least 12 firearms, split between the 3 ammo types should be in.
 More SPELLS: There's never too much ritual for the chamber! 80 Spells split between the 5 Spell schools.
 More enemies: I want to reach low double digits for the number of enemies in this game. They will ideally each post challenges in different ways, and hopefully push the Player to try out different tactics.
 Large open level design: The number of rooms in the map is still limited. Expect puzzle mechanics, hidden rooms and randomised (but balanced) loot spawns.
 Gun customisation: Optional, and not promised system. Though, ideally, I want the Player to be able to have more tools to solidify their builds in Ritual Chambers.
 Sigil Alchemy and Spell Combination: VERY OPTIONAL and also not promised. But, the idea of the Player having a way to craft their own Sigils and Spells, or combine Spell effects appeal to me very much. Realistically, though, this will require a lot of work and come with balancing concerns. Imagine it though...


If for some strange reason, you want to see more flashy spells, or you'd like to follow the game's progress much more closely, I turn you to the Ritual Chamber's various social media accounts, where we're more frequent with our updates.
https://www.tiktok.com/@ritualchambers
https://x.com/RitualChamber_
https://www.instagram.com/ritualchambers/
https://www.youtube.com/@RitualChamber

Otherwise, stay tuned for more devlogs and let's see how far we can take this project!

All the best!
B
Ritual Chambers Main Dev
